sections.h2: Transfer tax on a Wilmette sale
sections.html:
Wilmette levies its own real estate transfer tax: $3 for every $1,000 of consideration, or fraction of $1,000, under a 1988 village ordinance. The buyer is responsible for it, so it shows up on the buyer's side of the settlement statement. State law adds a separate tax on the transfer, which 35 ILCS 200/31-10 sets at 50 cents for each $500 of declared value.

The village will not release the stamps until the seller's utility account is clear, which ties buyer and seller together in the days before closing. Exempt transfers are filed under Chapter 9-15.6 of the village code, so review a trust transfer or similar deed with Finance before the closing date.

You or your representative must ask Finance for a final meter reading about two weeks before the date it is needed, by phone at 847-853-7607 or through the online request. The village confirms the request within two business days, and the read itself happens three business days before closing. Stamps are released once the seller and buyer have paid all outstanding bills.

Wilmette sale timeline
TimingWhoAction
Two weeks before the read dateSellerRequest the final meter reading
Within two business daysVillageConfirms the request and reports any open permit or inspection items
Three business days before closingVillagePerforms the final read
Before stamps issueSellerPays the final utility bill and other village balances such as parking tickets
Before closingBuyerSubmits the declaration form, pays the tax and prints the digital stamps

Two copies of the declaration go to the closing, and one copy with the stamps attached is filed with the Cook County Recorder of Deeds. A buyer claiming an exempt transfer under Chapter 9-15.6 of the village code must supply the same supporting documents filed with the Recorder.

sections.h2: Utility rates on the final bill
sections.html:
Wilmette bills water, sewer and refuse quarterly, so the final bill can include a partial quarter. The village lists these charges:

  • Water at $2.75 per 100 cubic feet.
  • Sewer at $4.40 per 100 cubic feet.
  • Refuse collection at $28.65 per month.
  • A quarterly meter fee set by meter size, from $0.67 for a 5/8 inch meter to $63.33 for a 4 inch meter.
  • A stormwater utility fee that varies by property.

The village is also switching out nearly 9,000 automated meter reading devices, and the meter replacement program covers meters 15 years of age and older. Ask Finance whether your property's meter is on the replacement list before the final read.

Wilmette is a high-priced market. The median owner-occupied value is $810,600, and 87.9% of homes are owner-lived. Median gross rent is $1,978 and median household income is $190,662. Population is estimated at 27,459 for July 2025, 2.5% below the 2020 base of 28,172, across 10,287 households averaging 2.66 people.

At that price level the village's report of open permit and inspection items matters, because an unresolved permit tends to surface just when a buyer is waiting on the stamps.

Wilmette sits in New Trier Township in Cook County. The township, which also covers Glencoe, Winnetka, Kenilworth and parts of Glenview and Northfield, was reassessed in 2025, and total assessed value grew 39%. The Cook County Assessor put the 2024 median single-family sale price at $1,314,000 against a median market value estimate of $1,186,000 for that class.

Cook County reassesses one-third of the county every year. Request your latest bill from the Cook County Treasurer before listing, and expect the title company to prorate the tax at closing.

The village runs a Green Homes Incentive Program that makes one-time payments to owners for eligible sustainable home installations. Its Comprehensive Plan also calls for a Historic Preservation Plan for preserving and rehabilitating historic homes.

Wilmette plans a $44.84 million capital program for 2026, focused on roads and water systems, so street or water main work may be under way near a listing. Building permit questions go to the Community Development Department at 847-853-7550.

A rental sale follows the same stamp and final read rules, but the village adds a few account details. Landlords are asked to tell Finance when a property is leased, so the village can inform both landlord and tenant about account issues. For a tenant moving out, the final meter read is done on the first available business day closest to the move-out date, and rental service requests are submitted online with the property address and request type.

If you are selling with a tenant in the home, coordinate the move-out date and the closing date with Finance, because the owner's final read for a sale is a separate request from a tenant's. New homeowners should also contact Finance to set up the water account in the right name.

Public elementary schools belong to Wilmette Public Schools District 39, with Marie Murphy School in Avoca District 37, and high school students attend New Trier High School. The CTA Purple Line ends at Linden Avenue, and Metra's Union Pacific North service stops at Green Bay Road. The village sits on Lake Michigan about 14 miles north of the Loop, and buyers weigh the trains and the schools first.

Once you have a signed contract, book the final meter read, pay the last utility bill and any parking tickets, and get your payoff letter. The buyer files the declaration and prints the stamps, and the title company sends the stamped copy to the Cook County Recorder of Deeds after closing.

A cash buyer shortens the path because no lender has to approve a loan, but the village steps do not go away. Start with the meter request, since the two-week lead time is the longest wait on the list.

Gather the paperwork in one folder: your latest Cook County tax bill, the payoff letter, any permit records, and a note of the final meter read date. If a permit is still open, ask Community Development how to close it out, because the village reports open items back to Finance when the read is requested. Sellers who wait until the last week often find the stamps delayed by a small unpaid balance, so ask Finance for a total a few days early and pay it right away.

faqs.q: Who pays the Wilmette transfer tax?
faqs.a: The buyer. The village charges $3 for every $1,000 of consideration, or fraction of $1,000, and the buyer buys the stamps. The seller's part is to pay the final utility bill so the stamps can be released.

faqs.q: How early do I request a final meter reading in Wilmette?
faqs.a: Request it about two weeks before the date it is needed. Finance confirms within two business days, and the read takes place three business days before closing.

faqs.q: Where do the Wilmette transfer stamps go?
faqs.a: Two copies of the declaration go to the closing. One copy, with the stamps affixed, is filed with the Cook County Recorder of Deeds. The village can issue the stamps digitally for printing.
Yes. New Trier Township, which includes Wilmette, was reassessed in 2025. Cook County reassesses one-third of the county each year.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Wilmette?
faqs.a: Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $810,600 for 2020 to 2024. Median household income is $190,662 and 87.9% of homes are owner-occupied.
